sandhi_response: When you are already feeling left behind academically, seeing others look effortlessly perfect can make you feel completely disconnected from your own body and life. Please be gentle with yourself today; you are navigating a highly demanding phase, and survival looks different for everyone.

user_input: I spent the entire semester sitting in the library coding for DSA labs and eating whatever oily mess the mess committee served. Now placements are starting next week, and everyone is buying these sharp, slim-fit formal suits and looking so incredibly put together. I tried on my old formal shirt today and the buttons were literally straining across my stomach; I looked in the mirror and just started crying. My flatmate is a 9.5 CGPA guy who also runs 5ks every morning, and here I am, bloated, fat, with dark circles, looking like a total wreck. How am I supposed to walk into an interview panel looking like this when everyone else looks like a model?
sandhi_response: It is incredibly heavy to feel like your body is being judged alongside your hard-earned skills, especially when you have poured so much of your physical energy into surviving this grueling semester. Your worth and the brilliant mind that solved those coding labs do not shrink just because a piece of fabric feels tight right now.

user_input: We took a group photo after the last end-sem exam and someone posted it on the batch WhatsApp group today. I feel sick to my stomach just looking at it. Everyone else looks so lean, happy, and vibrant, and I just look like a massive, shapeless blob standing in the corner trying to hide behind someone else. I’ve gained 12 kgs since starting my prep for competitive exams, living on instant noodles and stress. I literally want to delete WhatsApp and never show my face in the lecture hall again; I feel so disgusting and inferior compared to them.
sandhi_response: Seeing yourself through a lens of deep exhaustion makes it so easy to forget that this body has been carrying the immense weight of your survival and academic pressure. Let’s take a deep breath together and remember that a single, static photo cannot capture the depth of who you are or define your right to occupy space.

user_input: My mom called today and instead of asking how my mock tests went, she started talking about my cousin who just got placed at a FAANG company. Then she casually dropped, 'You should start eating less rice, you're gaining weight and it won't look good when we start looking for matches or when you go to office.' I felt this immediate wave of heat and nausea. I'm already dying trying to keep my CGPA above 8, and now even my physical body is a massive disappointment to my family compared to everyone else in our relative circle.
sandhi_response: It is deeply painful when the people who should be your safe harbor turn their expectations onto your physical form while you are already working so hard to stay afloat. Your body is not a product to be packaged for approval, but a living, breathing home that deserves kindness, especially from yourself.

user_input: Everyone in my hostel wing is suddenly into 'bulking' and going to the campus gym, tracking macros, and showing off their progress. I tried going with them, but I felt so weak and small, like a child among men. My arms are like twigs and my chest is completely flat, while they all have these broad shoulders and talk about their protein intake. I can't even focus on my DSA labs anymore because every time I look in the mirror, I just feel this overwhelming sense of inadequacy and shame that I don't look like a 'real' guy.
sandhi_response: The pressure to mold your body into a specific standard of strength can make you feel entirely invisible in your own skin. Your masculinity and your worth do not reside in the size of your frame, but in the quiet resilience you show every single day.

user_input: I have my college fest coming up next week, and my friends wanted to go shopping for matching outfits. I went to the changing room with a size M shirt, and it wouldn't even go past my shoulders, let alone button up. I had to ask the sales assistant for an XL while my friends were all laughing and trying on slim-fit clothes outside. I felt like crying right there in the trial room. I ended up making an excuse about a pending assignment and ran back to my hostel room; I'm seriously thinking of skipping the fest entirely because I can't bear the thought of standing next to them in photos.
sandhi_response: Squeezing ourselves into clothes—and social spaces—that don't fit can make us feel like we are the ones who are broken, rather than the standards themselves. You deserve to experience the joy of the fest without your physical form being the price of admission; your presence is valuable exactly as you are.

user_input: I had my first offline placement interview today. I spent hours prepping DSA and system design, but the moment I stood in front of the mirror in this cheap formal shirt I bought, I just wanted to melt into the floor. The buttons are straining, my face looks so bloated from all the late-night Maggi while coding, and everyone else in the placement cell lobby looked so sharp, fit, and effortless. I couldn't even make eye contact with the interviewer because I was so convinced they were judging how sloppy and out of shape I look, rather than my actual coding skills. I bombed the live coding round because my mind was just screaming about how huge I looked in that chair.
sandhi_response: It is incredibly heavy to carry the weight of self-judgment when you are already putting so much energy into stepping into a high-pressure interview. Your worth and the brilliant mind that solved those coding problems are not defined by how a piece of fabric sits on you in a stressful room.

user_input: Everyone in my batch is posting their summer internship photos on LinkedIn and Instagram, and they all look so perfectly toned, tanned, and aesthetic in their corporate casuals. Meanwhile, my CGPA dropped to 6.8, I've gained 12 kilos from stress-eating during end-sems, and I look like a thumb. I literally skipped the class group photo today because I couldn't bear the thought of my double chin being preserved forever in the department archives next to all these gym-goers. I feel like an academic failure and a physical eyesore, like I'm failing at college in every possible dimension.
sandhi_response: It makes complete sense that you'd want to hide when you feel like your body is carrying all the unspoken stress of your academic struggles. Please remember that your body has been working overtime to protect you and keep you safe through sleepless nights and heavy sems, even if it doesn't look like an Instagram feed right now.

user_input: My parents came down for the convocation prep and the first thing my dad said wasn't congrats on the TCS offer, it was 'You've really let yourself go, look at your cousin Rohan, he's so lean and cracked the 20LPA package'. I spent the whole night in my hostel bathroom crying and pinching my waist. I feel so disgusting. I worked 14-hour days to get this backlog cleared and get placed, but all they see is my stomach hanging over my jeans, and now I don't even want to walk across the stage to get my degree.
sandhi_response: It is deeply painful when the people who should be celebrating your hard-won victories reduce your immense academic effort to your physical appearance. Your worth is not a comparative math problem, and you deserve to walk across that stage holding your head high for the sheer resilience it took to get here.

user_input: I can't even go to the mess anymore. Every time I walk in, I feel like everyone is watching me load my plate, comparing how much I eat with how fat I am. There's this group of girls from the design department who always look like runway models, effortlessly skinny, and I'm just this blocky CS student who lives in oversized hoodies to hide my love handles. I ended up skipping lunch today and just survived on black coffee to avoid the stares. My brain is so foggy I can't even focus on my compiler design lab, but the fear of being seen and judged is paralyzing.
sandhi_response: Starving your body to escape the perceived judgment of others only leaves you running on empty when you need your strength the most. Let's take a deep breath together and remember that you have every right to nourish yourself and occupy space in that mess hall, just as you are.

user_input: I got selected for the college cultural fest dance team, but during the first costume trial today, they didn't have my size for the performance outfits. I felt so exposed and humiliated, especially when I saw my reflection next to the lead dancers who are literally half my size.
